note: ANSWERED STATICALLY, and the supplied addresses are the wrong kind of thing. (1) 02CF6678 IS NOT A DESCRIPTOR - IT IS AN MSVC THREAD-SAFE-STATIC GUARD. Its containing function 00617E60 calls _Init_thread_header (008092FC) and _Init_thread_footer (0080929C) and atexit (00808B90), and every one of the four addresses shows the same four-instruction idiom around it: `cmp dword [X], eax` (eax = the init epoch), `lea rcx, [X]`, `call _Init_thread_header`, `cmp dword [X], -1`. That is a 4-byte guard variable. Reading +0x30 from it as a class-name char* reads unrelated adjacent static bytes, which is exactly the 0x10 your control rejected - your control was right and the input was wrong. (2) THE MAPPING CORRECTION, and it is regular: THE OBJECT IS AT GUARD MINUS 0x58. There are four statics on a 0x60 stride - objects 02CF6560, 02CF65C0, 02CF6620, 02CF6680, guards 02CF65B8, 02CF6618, 02CF6678, 02CF66D8 - and 00617E60 touches each pair identically (guard: cmp/lea/cmp/lea; object: a single `lea rcx` before the constructor call). So the object for your CD3D11_BLEND_DESC guard 02CF6678 is 02CF6620, and the same minus-0x58 rule resolves the other three. (3) WHY NO STATIC READ CAN GO FURTHER: all of it is in the BSS TAIL of .data (section va 01DF0000, virtual size 0x11A7530, raw size 0x18E400), so these bytes are ZERO IN THE FILE and exist only at runtime. That is why these four hierarchy rows are unobserved in a static map - not because the map is wrong, but because there is nothing there to read until startup runs. (4) THE PHYRE LINK IS THE REGISTRY, NOT THE STATIC'S ADDRESS: 00617E7B does `lea rcx, [02CF1540]; call 006388C0`, and 006388C0 is the name lookup this store already documents as PType_FindOrRegisterByName, which reads its argument's +0x30 as a char*. So 02CF1540 is a PClass descriptor - and it is ALSO in BSS. The four 0x60 statics are built separately by 00632960 and are not themselves class descriptors; a PClass descriptor is at least 0x138 bytes by the contract's own layout and these are 0x58. Member/other metadata is the right reading, as you suspected.
